Dan Besbris listed Ace Bailey as a top-100 season-long pickup because Jaren Jackson Jr. is out, which opens up minutes for him. Bailey played 27 minutes in his last game on 11/18.

Brice Sensabaugh played the whole fourth quarter Tuesday and scored 25 of his 40 points in it as Utah pulled away from the Clippers. His bench minutes have climbed four straight games with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out, but Utah has not posted its report for tonight's back-to-back at the Lakers.
Peterson played only 19 minutes because he picked up four fouls, after playing at least 31 minutes in each of his previous four games. The show said he is in a funk but it is not too worried.
The show said the Jazz do not appear to like Collier and are not giving him real minutes. He played only 10 minutes on Nov. 18. The show said that could change only if Utah goes into full tank mode.

The show said Jaren Jackson Jr. is probably out at least another month; he has not played since October 26. The show said he will come back to a crowded Utah offense, with Darryn Peterson playing much better and Keyonte George taking a lot of shots.
Dan Besbris listed Jaxson Hayes as a top-100 season-long pickup because Jusuf Nurkic and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out, which opens up minutes for him. Hayes played 25 minutes in his last game on 11/18.
Josh Green got the start for Utah and played 28 minutes, his most since November 10. The show said fantasy players can ignore it.
Josh Okogie scored all nine of his points in the fourth quarter Tuesday as part of the bench group that pulled away from the Clippers; he played 10 of the quarter's 12 minutes.

Jusuf Nurkic has not played this season and has no clear return date. The show said he will start eventually but could be held to about 24 or 25 minutes, with a slow ramp-up. It said Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba have played well at center in his absence.
Keyonte George played 35 minutes Tuesday, two days after spraining his right ankle, and Utah's Wednesday game at the Lakers is the second night of a back-to-back.

Filipowski has fallen out of the Utah rotation even with three centers injured, playing two minutes on 11/13 and not playing on 11/15. The show said Utah cannot really play him right now because he cannot move well enough.
He is ruled out tonight (right hand fracture). Bailey gets fed the ball.
Dan Besbris listed Mo Bamba as a player he is still assessing because Jusuf Nurkic and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out, which opens up minutes for him. Bamba played 23 minutes in his last game on 11/18.

Svi Mykhailiuk played 34 minutes off the bench on Nov. 18 while rookie Darryn Peterson played only 19. The show said Mykhailiuk seemed to be playing in place of Peterson at times, which made it unsure what Utah was doing with the rotation.

Bradley is Utah's backup center behind Mo Bamba with the other centers out, and he has played 12 to 14 minutes in each of his last three games. The show said he does not project well, but he has the most natural path to extra minutes if Bamba gets hurt or cannot stay on the floor.

Dybantsa played 38 minutes and posted 23 points and 12 rebounds on 11/18 while making no threes. The show said he scores by getting to the rim and likes his 11/20 matchup against a Chicago team that it says allows the most paint points in the league.
Alex Sarr played just 22 minutes but still posted a useful line. The show said his minutes have been all over the place this season.

Anthony Davis has played legitimate starter minutes lately, with 35 and 34 minutes in his last two games and a 44-minute game on 11/12. The show said he is producing about 1.33 DraftKings points per minute and called his 11/20 matchup against a fast, poor Chicago defense the best spot among the top-salary players.
Bilal Coulibaly returned on Nov. 11 after missing Nov. 9 and played 25 minutes off the bench. The show said he is off the injury report and offers steals, blocks and a few assists.
The show said Justin Champagnie has a broken foot and should return around the All-Star break, and he has not played since Oct. 26.

The show said Kyshawn George has held a 22.5% usage rate and 21% assist rate at about one DraftKings point per minute, which is close to Trae Young's per-minute rate. The show said George is outplaying AJ Dybantsa per minute at a similar price, and that Dybantsa's biggest issue is sharing the ball with Anthony Davis and Trae Young. George has started and played 30, 38 and 40 minutes in his last three games.

Trae Young is in a deep shooting slump, but he has kept playing 32 to 33 minutes as Washington's starter, and the team snapped a long losing streak. The show said his minutes and shots are not wavering, so it expects his efficiency to bounce back.

Johnson played only eight minutes and did not score on Wednesday, after playing about 30 minutes as recently as Nov. 12. The show called him a bust so far and said Will Riley is also back in the rotation but playing poorly.

Will Riley scored 17.2 of his 20.8 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 28-point loss against HOU on Sunday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
